title: Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Sparks $120M+ Box Office Revival, Says Hollywood Reporter
body:
The latest installment of the long‑running dystopian saga, *The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping*, has surged past the $120 million mark worldwide, signaling a robust revival for the franchise after a comparatively quiet 2023. Opening in more than 4,000 North American venues, the film posted a $56 million domestic haul on its first day, delivering the fourth‑best opening Friday ever recorded for the series and positioning Lionsgate for one of its strongest box‑office seasons in recent memory.

The numbers arrive at a pivotal moment for the brand, which has struggled to maintain momentum since the prequel *The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes* underperformed at the box office and received mixed critical reception. By contrast, *Sunrise on the Reaping* taps into the nostalgia of the original trilogy while introducing fresh narrative threads that appear to resonate with both longtime fans and a new generation of viewers. The film’s marketing campaign leaned heavily on the promise of “the next chapter” for Katniss Everdeen’s legacy, a strategy that has evidently paid dividends in ticket sales and social‑media buzz.

Industry analysts attribute the strong debut to several converging factors. First, the timing of the release—early summer, when audiences are eager for blockbuster experiences—has provided a natural lift. Second, Lionsgate’s decision to roll out the movie across a record‑high number of screens in the United States and Canada has maximized accessibility, ensuring that even smaller markets can contribute to the opening day totals. Finally, the franchise’s strategic use of cross‑platform promotion, including a viral TikTok challenge and a partnership with a major streaming service for exclusive behind‑the‑scenes content, has amplified word‑of‑mouth momentum far beyond traditional advertising channels.

Critically, the film has garnered a mixed but generally favorable response. Reviewers have praised the visual spectacle, particularly the expanded arena designs and the heightened stakes of the new “Reaping” ceremony, while noting that the script occasionally leans on familiar tropes. Nevertheless, the performances of the returning cast members—especially the lead actress portraying a grown‑up Katniss—have been highlighted as a key draw, delivering emotional depth that bridges the series’ past and present. Audience exit polls suggest that the blend of action, political commentary, and character evolution struck a chord, reinforcing the franchise’s relevance in a cultural climate increasingly attuned to themes of resistance and societal inequity.

From a financial perspective, the $120 million global total—achieved within the first week—places *Sunrise on the Reaping* on a trajectory to become the highest‑grossing entry in the series, surpassing the $150 million benchmark set by the original *Mockingjay – Part 2*. If the current pace holds, the film could comfortably breach the $200 million mark worldwide, a milestone that would not only vindicate Lionsgate’s investment but also revive confidence in mid‑budget franchise filmmaking amid an industry dominated by superhero juggernauts.

Looking ahead, the box‑office surge sets the stage for a potentially lucrative sequel pipeline, as Lionsgate has already hinted at plans for a seventh film that will explore the aftermath of the Reaping and the emergence of a new political order. With merchandising, streaming rights, and international markets poised to contribute further revenue, the franchise appears to be on a resurgence path that could redefine its place in contemporary popular culture. The coming months will reveal whether *Sunrise on the Reaping* can sustain its momentum and solidify a lasting comeback for a series that once seemed to be winding down.
